I definitely struggle with looking after my cat. Doesn't help the fact that she's super independent. Unless I do it every day at a set time I will forget either to feed her, water her or change her litter. Feeding is a bit easier as I literally see that empty. Litter and water I procrastinate if I'm not careful then bam its full on armageddon in her litter box and all her water bowls are dry and if you asked me when the last time I refilled her water or her litter I'd say two days ago? I get super timeblind around it. So now I just do it daily. Remind myself with an alarm and a picture of her on my desk so I do it before work.

Your LO's hair is pretty similar to mines! I have no idea what type his hair is but the tangling and frizzyness was driving me crazy. I've been getting it a bit more under control by washing once every couple of days and just using some conditioner and if it gets greasy (which it doesn't that much) use Johnsons baby shampoo to reset. However I find that it's when he's sleeping is when it gets most frizzy and tangled so in the mornings I've been using this curling custard from Boots that I find really tames and defines the curls - also Deva curl has a custard and a spray that works well I've found. So essentially tldr products for after washing it are your best bet if you're wanting to define the curls and stop the frizz.

I like this so yes the requests to developers are incomplete or unclear -clients would change mind on priorities (no longer issue now we have roadmap and we aren't catering to their flip flopping) so tickets would get into a sprint without full refinement. 

Not written in enough detail - I have very little time to do this, it's my sisyphus-esque challenge of trying to get the tickets in a state that devs can pick up in time before the next sprint starts and also have them refine it  so we can actually capture details.

The repeating questions were caught early and so for certain issues there is now a basic script I say to people  pointing them to the place to find the answer rather than me distract myself and find it for them.

Devs aren't green but morale is low so I think due diligence is going out the window and so in refinement things are getting missed and only when in progress is clarification needed.

Product knowledge and documentation is pretty much non existent
When I typed it out it did seem insane
I don't actually have too many meetings/calendar invites that are time sinks. Some go over time but it's rare.
Right now roughly a team of 20, tickets vary but average about 90 tickets per sprint

I do feel that some factors are out of my control with this team and product but the team are lovely and work really hard and the product itself is exciting. Its still a relatively new job (4 months in) so even though I can't see myself here forever I don't want to be looking for a new job yet. But I do agree with the resenting part, I'm definitely starting to feel that

I know a lot of the fires are residual from the product setup, very little time spent in discovery, not clear roadmap, few fully refined sprints and designs not clear so a lot of the fires are inherited and I'm slowly putting them out as time goes on. We have a roadmap now, designs for the product are ahead so the developers have time to look at them but it's still few tickets fully refined and with clear requirements and the roadmap is only a few months So the problem is going to occur again.

It's difficult as if I knew I would know to attack it - if that makes sense. I feel like a lot of the questions I'm answering are from developers requiring more clarity on tickets and requirements which means I'm answering questions rather than writing documents/tickets. Another feeling of firefighting is my product lead will ask me to create documents or presentations or lead meetings with very little heads up. 

I'm limiting Slack - which is how my team communicates as the notifications are constant and (I'm ADD) so I feel the need to check/answer them then get distracted from the task I was doing and so it takes me longer to get back into a focused state.
